subject: Acme Corp DPA - redlines, subprocessors & transfer approach
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <privacy@acme.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Acme Corp DPA - redlines, subprocessors & transfer approach

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for moving this forward. Attached is our initial DPA redline (Acme_DPA_Redline_v1.docx). Three items we want to confirm up front so we can converge quickly: 

1) Subprocessor notice timeline: your draft requests a 30-day prior notice for new subprocessors plus consent rights. We'd like to propose a notification window (30 days) with an objection window limited to 14 days and an automatic deemed consent if no objection is raised — this aligns with our standard practice.

2) Transfers: we included a clause referencing EU SCCs + a UK Addendum as the mechanism; please confirm Acme is OK with SCCs being executed via a separate signature page (standard for DocuSign flow) and that you don't require bespoke data localization commitments.

3) Audit & incident windows: your team flagged a 10-business-day preservation period in the incident language; we redlined to 30 days and requested clarifying the scope of onsite audits to avoid operational disruption.

Action items from our side: Monica will attach our current subprocessor roster and security attestations. Kimberly — appreciate your legal guidance on anything we should absolutely refuse.

If the high-level approach above is acceptable, can you route the counsel redline back to us this week? We can then push to DocuSign.

Thanks —
Rishi
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
redwood.com

Attachments: Acme_DPA_Redline_v1.docx (docx)

From: Samantha Lee <privacy@acme.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Procurement <procurement@acme.com>
Date: 2026-11-16T11:43:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Acme Corp DPA - redlines, subprocessors & transfer approach

Hi Rishi —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Please see our counsel comments attached (Acme_DPA_Counsel_Comments.pdf) — high level: we can accept SCCs + UK Addendum as the transfer mechanism, but a few points need clearer language or pushback from your side: 

- Subprocessor notice/consent: Our legal team requires affirmative consent for new subprocessors if they will process personal data of Acme EU subjects. The 14-day objection window with deemed consent won’t work for certain categories (e.g., security vendors, or subprocessors in scope of critical infrastructure). Can you confirm which categories you would carve out?

- Right to audit: We need to preserve a right to an annual audit by an accredited third party, with 30 days' notice. Onsite audits are rare; remote assessments are preferred.

- Deletion & return: We're insisting on a 60-day deletion/return period post-termination for archived backups. Your redline at 30 days is shorter than we expect.

- Incident notification: 24 hours for initial notification plus a root-cause update within 14 days.

I've highlighted suggested alternative language in the attached PDF and inserted a few comments in the subprocessor section to ask for your current roster and whether subprocessors perform any profiling/automated decision-making for Acme data.

If you'd like, we can set a short call between our privacy counsel and Kimberly to walk through the open items.

Best,
Samantha Lee
Senior Privacy Counsel, Acme Corp

Attachment: Acme_DPA_Counsel_Comments.pdf (pdf)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <privacy@acme.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-17T08:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Acme Corp DPA - redlines, subprocessors & transfer approach

Thanks Samantha — and thank you Rishi for circulating. Quick legal take: 

- Subprocessors: We should accept an affirmative consent model for high-risk categories but push back on blanket affirmative consent for routine infra/subscription services. Proposed compromise: 30-day notice; Acme can object within 14 days for a stated reason; for any objection that we cannot remediate, offer an escalation to a limited mitigation plan (e.g., additional contractual or technical safeguards). This preserves buyer protections while avoiding deal-stopping veto power.

- Audit: Accept remote third-party audits annually with a right to request an onsite follow-up only upon reasonable suspicion of non-compliance. Onsite should be limited and subject to reasonable confidentiality and scope restrictions. We should not accept unconditional onsite audits.

- Deletion/Return: 60 days is aggressive for backups, propose 45 days for backups + 30 days for primary data. If Acme insists, we can accept 60 days for narrow categories but push for operational exceptions (e.g., legal hold).

- Incident windows: 24-hour initial notification is reasonable — we can commit to that. Root-cause within 14 days is acceptable as long as it is qualified as "reasonably practicable" and supplemented by periodic updates.

I'll prepare redline responses for each comment in our next pass. Monica, can you confirm whether any subprocessors do profiling/automated decision-making for Acme data? If yes, we need to mark that as sensitive.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T10:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Acme Corp DPA - redlines, subprocessors & transfer approach

Hi — following up with the subprocessor roster and quick confirmations: 

Attached: current roster (inline below):
- Cloud infra: AWS (us-east-1 / eu-west-1) — data-at-rest encryption, standard contract terms via AWS DPA.
- Observability: Datadog (logs only, no personalization), SSO through SAML.
- Model hosting cache/kv: FastKV Inc. (managed), performs tokenization and transient KV storage — no profiling.
- Payment processor: Stripe (customer billing) — no EU subject PII processing for Acme scope.
- Customer support tooling: SupportDesk Co. (transcripts, may contain customer data).

None of our current subprocessors perform automated profiling on Acme data for decision-making that affects individuals. FastKV handles ephemeral caching and we can add SIEM-level access logs to show no profiling.

I will upload our latest security attestations and SOC summary to the secure link.

Monica
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Related link: https://drive.redwood.com/Acme/subprocessors (internal)

Samantha / Acme team —

Thanks for the detailed comments and Kimberly/Monica for the quick triage. Based on the discussion above we propose the following path: 

1) We'll produce a second redline that: (a) accepts SCCs + UK Addendum, (b) revises subprocessor language to 30-day notice + 14-day objection with escalation pathway, (c) accepts 24-hour incident notification and "root-cause update within 14 days where reasonably practicable", and (d) proposes 45-day backup deletion (with limited exceptions).

2) I will upload the next redline to DocuSign with a cover page that lists the agreed items and a signature block for Acme and Redwood. Please expect the DocuSign envelope at the link below. If these terms are acceptable at a high level, we ask Acme to sign the DocuSign envelope to avoid further delay.
